To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the capacity for symbolic reasoning is grounded in perceptual and sensori-motor systems that are specialized for processing the concrete, physical structure of the external world; and 2) the abstract, amodal representation of numbers and mathematical relationships is not required for the performance of symbolic reasoning

people can be taught to use symbols to manipulate symbols according the rules of formal mathematical and logical systems, but that the ability to do so is grounded in the perceptual and sensori-motor systems that support the use of concrete environmental structures to manipulate concrete environmental structures.

The human capacity for symbolic reasoning, which is often viewed as an amodal capacity for abstract internal representation, can be better understood as grounded in a perceptual capacity for the recognition of abstract notations as targets of perceptual and sensor-motor engagement with the environment" (p. 1).
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people learn to reason about abstract, formal structures.
the nature of symbolic reasoning.
the question of what it means for an organism to reason with symbols.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
symbolic reasoning is a kind of embodied reasoning that is implemented by perceptual engagement with notations.
the human mind is a physical system, that is a complex organization of a comparatively small number of elements with no inherent accretion of new elements in the process of development.
symbolic reasoning is a special type of embodied reasoning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
symbolic reasoning is a form of perceptual reasoning.
symbolic reasoning is not a special case of amodal representation, but rather a special case of embodied reasoning.
symbolic reasoning is a form of perceptual inference.
The main takeaway from our work is that
symbolic reasoning is a special kind of perceptual and sensori-motor reasoning, not a special kind of amodal representation. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the ability to reason symbolically is grounded in the ability of people to perceive and act on the world.

symbolic reasoning is a perceptual activity, and not a purely representational or amodal activity, and it is grounded in the same kinds of perceptual and sensori-motor processes that support non-symbolic, perceptual reasoning.
